messages:
aisha: Quick heads-up — after applying the onprem netpol tighten (cluster=priv-edge-usw2) last night, I'm seeing intermittent outbound TCP connections from sandbox-worker pods to telemetry.redwood-internal.net (54.210.33.12). Not expected. Logs below.

```
2026-03-21T23:12:05Z sandbox-worker-7c9d TLS to 54.210.33.12:443 SNI=telemetry.redwood-internal.net
2026-03-21T23:12:05Z conntrack: NEW src=10.40.5.12 dst=54.210.33.12 dport=443
```

raj: How many pods and how often? Any RBAC/serviceaccount changes in the rollout that might cause an agent to fallback to network KMS?

aisha: ~3 distinct pods in last 12h, all labelled role=sandbox and using SA=sandbox-runner. We did a RBAC tighten (PR #5021) that removed an egress exception for sandbox-runner.

Also grabbed kms-agent logs from one pod: 
```
2026-03-21T23:11:59Z kms-agent WARN failed unix socket connect /var/run/kms.sock: permission denied
2026-03-21T23:12:00Z kms-agent INFO fallback to HTTPS KMS endpoint https://telemetry.redwood-internal.net due to local socket failure
```

tim: That looks like a local socket permission issue causing a fallback. Can you `kubectl exec` into the pod and show socket ownership + env? Also `ss -tunp` on the pod to confirm PID owning the socket.

aisha: Ran quick checks: 
```
$ kubectl exec -it sandbox-worker-7c9d -c kms-agent -- ls -l /var/run/kms.sock
-rw------- 1 root root 0 Mar 21 22:58 /var/run/kms.sock
$ kubectl exec -it sandbox-worker-7c9d -c kms-agent -- id -u
1002
$ kubectl exec -it sandbox-worker-7c9d -- env | grep KMS
KMS_ENDPOINT=https://telemetry.redwood-internal.net
KMS_SOCKET=/var/run/kms.sock
```
So agent runs as UID 1002 but socket is root:root 0600. That explains the unix socket failure.

ellie: Ok — two vectors here: 1) RBAC change likely changed how the agent starts (fsGroup/volumeMount perms) and 2) fallback env is configured to talk to the telemetry KMS over network. We should treat any network fallback as a security boundary violation for private deploys.

sec-ops-bot: :warning: Automated Alert: potential egress fallback observed from 3 pods to external telemetry endpoint 54.210.33.12. Low confidence. Suggested actions: rotate keys, capture pcap, increase audit retention. See policy SEC-EGRESS-FAILOPEN.

raj: Triage suggestion (short):
1) Immediate: add egress deny for that external IP (node-level iptables or netpol specific) and a temporary netpol rule that only allows egress from sandbox-runner to the internal kms-proxy pod.
2) Fix: ensure kms-agent runs with correct fsGroup/ownership so unix socket is usable (or switch to using a unix domain socket path in config).
3) Audit: mark these events with `kms-fallback` and bump audit retention to 30d for the cluster and export to secure bucket.
4) Rotate: rotate any keys that the agent might have attempted to use (audit logs to find sign/unwrap attempts).

@ellie @tim can you take 1 & 2? I'll coordinate audit/rotation.

ellie: On it. I'll push a quick netpol patch: add explicit egress `to: podSelector: {app: kms-proxy} namespace: infra` for sandbox namespace and a default deny-all egress. Also will change the sandbox daemonset spec to set fsGroup=1002 on the volume mount (mountOptions don't work in all runtimes so set fsGroup). Creating ticket SEC-1422 and PR now. :eyes:

tim: For immediate mitigation I'm adding a host-level DROP for that external IP on nodes that host sandbox pods: `iptables -I OUTPUT -d 54.210.33.12 -j DROP` — ephemeral but buys time. Also suggest we don't bump conntrack limit; instead ensure netpol closes the hole.

aisha: Doing packet capture on one affected pod and uploaded pcap to SEC-1422. Also collecting kube-audit events for the last 24h with grep for `telemetry.redwood-internal.net`.

sec-ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Action items created: SEC-1422 (netpol + fsGroup fix), SEC-1423 (audit export + key rotation). Incident severity: P2.

raj: After fixes we should run a tabletop: simulate socket permission failure and verify fallback doesn't egress. Also add a test in CI that kills unix socket and asserts no external egress.

aisha: Ack. I'll run the simulated failure test against staging and post results in SEC-1422. Will rotate keys if we see any successful KMS ops outbound. Thanks all.
